negative_findings.description: None of the international trade titles in this cell (Finextra, The Paypers, PYMNTS, IBSi, Retail Banker International, FinTech Futures) appears to operate a Hungary-specific section or correspondent; Hungary coverage is event-driven and sparse, surfacing only when a large vendor issues a press release.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungary appears as a keyword tag (FinTech Futures) or as scattered articles, not as a maintained beat. Coverage clusters heavily on OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary, with almost nothing on mid-tier banks, savings cooperatives or merchant acquirers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This cell will under-report the Hungarian market by construction; it must be paired with Hungarian-language domestic media and MNB/regulatory filings rather than treated as a standalone view.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language search was run as required, but by definition this cell covers English-language international outlets; the Hungarian query surfaced only domestic sources (MNB fintech and digitalisation report, Portfolio.hu, FinTechZone, Magyar Bankszövetség press releases) that belong to other coverage cells, not international trade/analyst coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'magyar bank nemzetközi sajtó megállapodás technológiai szolgáltató fizetési piac elemzés' returned mnb.hu, portfolio.hu, bankszovetseg.hu, fintechzone.hu — all domestic. No Hungarian-language edition or Hungarian mirror of Finextra/The Paypers/PYMNTS/IBSi was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms there is no Hungarian-language on-ramp into the international trade titles; local-language monitoring cannot substitute for, and is not duplicated by, this cell.

negative_findings.description: No freely accessible analyst source was found that gives Hungarian market share by payments vendor or acquirer (terminal estate share, processing share, core-banking installed base).
negative_findings.result_summary: GlobalData, Euromonitor and Mordor abstracts give market sizing and, in Mordor's case, a vendor roster, but no share splits without purchase. IBSi's Sales League Table is paid and not Hungary-segmented in public view.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Competitive-position questions cannot be answered from this cell without a licensed purchase; expectations and budget should be set accordingly.

negative_findings.description: ITKeyMedia and Emerging Europe were probed as possible additional English-language CEE outlets covering Hungarian banking technology; neither returned Hungary payments/banking coverage in the results obtained.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned The Recursive, Finovate and FinTech Futures instead; no ITKeyMedia result appeared at all.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These should be re-probed directly on their own site search before being written off — a single search miss is not evidence of absence.

coverage_gaps.description: All candidates were identified from search-result metadata and article summaries; individual pages were not fetched, so paywall depth, robots.txt posture and archive completeness are unassessed. Finextra, PYMNTS and Statista are known to deploy bot defences that may return 403 to naive crawlers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic verification pass over every URL, and separately probe robots.txt plus one representative article per domain to classify paywall type (open / metered / registration / hard).

coverage_gaps.description: Several plausible international outlets in this cell were not reached in the searches performed: Electronic Payments International, The Banker, Central Banking, Nilson Report, Merchant Payments Ecosystem / PaymentsCMI, ATM Marketplace, Payments Dive, Sifted, and the S&P Global / Fitch / Moody's Hungarian bank sector commentary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted site-restricted searches per outlet for 'Hungary' and for the main Hungarian bank names (OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, CIB, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit, Magnet) to confirm whether each carries usable Hungarian coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Search-driven discovery in this cell skews to OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary. The merged MBH Bank (MKB + Budapest Bank + Takarékbank), K&H (KBC), CIB (Intesa), Raiffeisen Hungary, Gránit Bank, and domestic acquirers/PSPs (Barion, B-Payment Szolgáltató Zrt., SRS Informatika Kft., Cellum, OTP Mobil/Simple, QVIK) were barely represented.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-query each international outlet with the full Hungarian actor list including legal-form suffixes (Zrt., Nyrt., Kft.) and English aliases, rather than relying on the country name alone.

coverage_gaps.description: Retrievable items skew recent or to a few landmark deals (2014 OTPay, 2018-2019 instant payments, 2023 iGCB core banking, 2025-2026 items). Whether these outlets' archives are fully open and searchable back a decade is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test archive depth by paginating each outlet's Hungary keyword/search index to its oldest entry, and supplement with Wayback Machine snapshots where archives are truncated or reorganised.

coverage_gaps.description: The highest-value assets in this cell (GlobalData Hungary Cards and Payments to 2030, Euromonitor Financial Cards and Payments in Hungary, IBSi Sales League Table, Mordor Hungary POS Terminal) are all licensed products; no procurement decision or price discovery was made.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Price the four reports, check for existing institutional subscriptions (Passport, GlobalData Intelligence Center), and decide on one anchor purchase for market sizing plus free triangulation against MNB payment statistics.

brief: English-language international trade and analyst coverage of Hungary is real but thin and event-driven: Finextra (especially its vendor press-release channel), FinTech Futures' Hungary keyword feed, IBS Intelligence's news and case-study library, The Paypers, Retail Banker International and PYMNTS between them capture most major Hungarian bank technology selections, but almost exclusively for OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary. The distinctive value of the cell is that these outlets reprint vendor-supplied scope and module detail that Hungarian domestic media omit, so the highest-yield tactic is snowballing each trade article upstream to the originating vendor newsroom. For market sizing, no free source exists: GlobalData, Euromonitor, Mordor and Verified Market Research all gate Hungary payments/POS figures behind licences, though Mordor's public companies page usefully leaks a named Hungarian POS terminal vendor roster. This cell must be treated as an aggregation and translation layer over other cells, never as a standalone view of the Hungarian market.
